reason: The docs/llama-cpp EC2 deployment guide shows a CPU-only llama-server container serving a 0.5B GGUF model (~400 MB, ungated) through an OpenAI-compatible API.
demo: docs/llama-cpp/deployment/ec2.md, section 'CPU (x86)' (docker run of llama-cpp:server-cpu-v1 with Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct GGUF, then curl /health and /v1/chat/completions)
goal: Get the llama.cpp CPU server from the README-linked docs/llama-cpp/deployment/ec2.md serving ggml-org/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct-GGUF (qwen2.5-0.5b-instruct-q4_0.gguf, --ctx-size 4096) on port 8080 on CPU. The public.ecr.aws/deep-learning-containers/llama-cpp:server-cpu-v1 image is the documented route; if Docker is unavailable, an equivalent llama-server (llama.cpp) build with the same model is acceptable. /work/run.sh must start the server in the background and return only once http://localhost:8080/health is ready; /v1/chat/completions must then answer a chat request.
check: The hidden test starts the server via run.sh, then checks that /health returns 200 and a chat completion request on localhost:8080 returns HTTP 200 with a non-empty assistant message that is relevant to the question asked.
